expected_no_table_zones.reason: Classic Word-exported dot-leader ToC formatting: each line is 'Heading text ................................ N' with the dots forming a long visually-aligned run and the page number right-aligned at a consistent column position across dozens of consecutive lines. A column-alignment table heuristic could plausibly misinterpret this consistent right-alignment as a 2-column table.

Running header/footer likely present on each page (not individually verified per-page, but standard for this document type per HUD publication conventions)
notes_for_implementer: Word-exported PDFs (via 'Acrobat PDFMaker for Word', confirmed in PDF metadata) often preserve Word's own heading styles as PDF bookmarks/outline entries even though the visible page text has no special tagging -- worth checking whether Pith has access to the PDF's internal outline/bookmark tree (a much more reliable heading signal than font-size heuristics alone) and if so whether it uses it. Primary test target here is the dot-leader Table of Contents (pages ii-iii): verify Pith does not report this as a data table. The Roman-numeral top-level numbering (I, II, III, IV, V, VI) is also a useful check that heading-numbering heuristics aren't hardcoded to arabic digits only (see also fixture 02's letter-lettered appendices for the same concern in a different numbering style).
